executive_assessment.text: Jonglei, Lakes, Unity and contrasting western flood patterns add differentiated2025exposure; high-ground planting is described alongside flood timing, not as an isolated impact estimate.

Source-stated displacement/resource competition is broad and historical. Humanitarian routes, crop-assessment access and agricultural activity face distinct insecurity constraints and should not be conflated.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-12 reports: By November 2025, floods in Greater Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei had affected over 1.3 million people and displaced over 375,000, while northern and south-eastern regions faced prolonged dry spells; women and girls faced increased workloads and GBV exposure.
The2025 CFSAM reports Jonglei, Lakes and Unity accounted for88%of flood-affected people, while western Sudd, Tonj and Greater Bahr el Ghazal experienced less extensive flooding than prior years.

known_gaps.text: CCKP establishes future warming direction and precipitation uncertainty, but the bank still lacks a complete extraction of numeric p10, p50, and p90 temperature, precipitation, variability, and extreme-event projections across scenarios, horizons, seasons, and subnational areas.

Adaptive capacity is demonstrated only for selected social-protection beneficiaries and community institutions; evidence remains insufficient for national systems, climate-specific capabilities, durability, and excluded locations or groups.

Official project monitoring reports reach, functionality, and beneficiary outcomes, but no independent evaluation establishes causal effectiveness, delivery failure across the portfolio, durability, or unintended effects.
Dedicated evidence is missing for fisheries, forests, the Sudd wetland system, disability-differentiated vulnerability, and several states.
The HNRP's official OCHA page returned 403; the complete report was read from a third-party PDF mirror, whose cover and about-page identify the source as OCHA-consolidated.
The FAO DOI landing page for CFSAM returned 403; the full report PDF was accessible through the South Sudan CLIMIS portal.
Some CFSAM locations were too insecure for field teams; telephone and community-crop-monitoring reports reduce direct observation in those areas.
The 2026 FAO GIEWS brief is a 7 September snapshot; seasonal forecasts and security/market conditions may have changed by later 2026.

Climate-FCV material is strongest for flood-related displacement and resource competition in the HNRP's broad affected-area framing; it does not quantify local causal effects or establish uniform conflict outcomes.
The DTM August 2025 flood-displacement report was inaccessible; current subnational displacement detail beyond the accessible HNRP and CFSAM remains incomplete.
HNRP findings refer to2025conditions and were read from an identified OCHA-report mirror because the official landing page returned403.
